topic: The Economic Function of Gold : Preventing Inflation by Restricting Money Supply
passage: The big problem with money creating by the government is that those who run the government always faces the temptation to create less money and spend it.
Whether among ancient kings or modern politicians, this has happened again and again over the centuries, lead to inflation and the many economic and social problems that follow from inflation.
For this reason, many countries have been preferred using gold, silver, or some other material that is inherently unlimited in supply, as money.
It is a way of depriving governments [전치사] of the power to expand the money supply to inflationary levels.
Gold has long considered ideal for this purpose, since the supply of gold in the world usually cannot be increased slowly.
When paper money is convertible into gold whenever the individual chooses to do so, then the money says being "backed up" by gold.

This expression is misleading only if we imagine that the value of the gold is somehow transferring to the paper money, when in fact the real point is that the gold simply limits the amount of paper money that can issue.
